note:
Header banner batch for /pages/copper-peptide-research — Malcolm's concept, 2026-08-25: one scene combining BLUE COPPER PEPTIDE POWDER, laboratory glassware holding BLUE LIQUID, and a MICROSCOPE on a laboratory bench.

The live header there is skingenetix-research-copper-peptide-banner.jpg, a leftover from before the banner system existed. This wave replaces it with a frame built to the same rules as /pages/the-science, which shipped on 2026-08-24 from the blue-glassware wave — same graphite ground, same Clinical blue, same measured left type zone — so the science page and the ingredient-research pages read as one system rather than three unrelated pictures.

CLASS B, every slot. There is no product in frame, so there is nothing branded to protect and no reference is attached; per the art-direction doc the brief must therefore not be asked for identity at all, only for material. FLUX.2 is in the run for the same reason — it invents brand identities, and there is no branding here for it to invent.

THE POWDER IS DESCRIBED, NEVER NAMED. GHK-Cu really is a deep blue crystalline powder, but 'copper peptide powder' in a prompt hands every engine two nouns it will resolve its own way — 'copper' pulls the heap orange, 'peptide' pulls a molecular diagram into frame, and 'powder' pulls loose cosmetic makeup. So the brief asks for 'fine dry crystalline granules in a deep vivid blue' on a laboratory watch glass, and the negatives bar the makeup reading explicitly. (describe-the-thing-dont-name-it, four image faults with one root cause.)

THE LIQUID IS SPECIFIED, because nothing else specifies it. Serum and solution briefs come back milky white whenever the brief leaves the contents to the engine. Every vessel here states colour hex 014EB1, fill level, stillness and meniscus. (the-specs-never-describe-the-liquid.)

GLASSWARE IS ASKED FOR PLAIN, NOT GRADUATED. A graduated cylinder carries printed numerals, and asking for one while negating lettering is a brief that fights itself — the engine resolves the contradiction for you and usually garbles the digits. Plain unmarked glass is asked for in the prompt, and digits are negated in the same breath.

NEGATIVES DIVERGE FROM THE DOC'S CLASS B SET, deliberately. The blanket 'no bottle' is gone — glassware is the subject — and is replaced by the specific things not wanted: no dropper bottle, no cosmetic bottle, no packaging, no label, no logo, no lettering. 'No more than one subject' is gone too, because the brief asks for three. Both were dropped for the same reason on the 2026-08-24 microscope wave.

The blue is the palette's Clinical blue, hex 014EB1 — the Copper Peptide scene colour. Ground is graphite 1A1A1A.

Type zone is the LEFT 45 percent on all three, stated as a measured fraction of frame width because an object anchor does not hold across suppliers. That matches every banner published this week (heading left, subject right). NOTE for the publish step: this page currently CENTRES its heading, so whichever frame Malcolm picks, the section's text position moves centre-left the way /pages/the-science did.

Generated at the page-break band spec, 3072x1280 (2.4:1); gpt-image will land at 2048x848 because it caps there. The winner then goes through scripts/extend-banner-canvas.py to ~4.42:1 so full height survives a 1920 viewport in the theme's fixed-height header box — the left type zone is quiet defocused bench, which is the easy case for the extender.

defaults.negative_global: no dropper bottle, no cosmetic bottle, no serum bottle, no product packaging, no carton, no label, no logo, no brand mark, no lettering of any kind, no text, no numerals, no printed digits, no scale graduations with numbers, no watermark, no signature, no border, no collage, no multi-panel layout, not a flat-lay, no person, no hands, no face, no readable screens, no branded equipment, no makeup, no cosmetic compact, no pigment swatch, no eyeshadow, no botanicals, no leaves, no flowers, no wood, no linen, no lens flare, no neon glow, no sci-fi hologram, no molecular diagram, no chemical notation

slots.title: copper-peptide-research — A · bench wide, watch glass of blue powder, type zone left
slots.prompt:
Close-up laboratory photograph across a dark bench. One laboratory microscope in matte black and brushed stainless stands in the right third of the frame, between 68 and 96 percent of frame width, cropped by the top edge so only its stage, objective turret and lower body are in view — a close-up, not the whole instrument. On the bench in front of it, at roughly 46 to 66 percent of frame width, stand two pieces of plain unmarked clear laboratory glassware side by side: one low cylindrical beaker and one taller straight-sided glass cylinder, both holding a clear vivid blue liquid, colour hex 014EB1, filled about two thirds. The glass is thin and precise, the liquid perfectly still with a clean meniscus, and the key light passes through it so the blue glows and throws a soft blue pool of light onto the bench beneath.

Nearest to camera, at roughly 34 to 48 percent of frame width and low in the frame, a shallow round clear glass laboratory dish holds a small conical heap of fine dry crystalline granules in a deep vivid blue, colour hex 014EB1 — dense, faceted, catching the key light grain by grain like coarse salt, sitting in a tidy mound with a few loose grains on the glass around it. This heap is the sharpest thing in the picture.

The bench and ground are deep graphite, colour hex 1A1A1A, falling to near black at the edges, so the blue is the only colour in the frame. One hard key light from the upper left rakes the stainless and edges the glassware; one soft fill. The left 45 percent of the frame, measured from 0 to 45 percent of frame width, is quiet defocused bench held at even tone and low detail so a headline can sit on it unaided. Shot at f/4 on a 50mm, clinical, cold, precise.
slots.negative_extra: no eyepieces pointing at camera, no coloured stains on slides, no rulers, no notebooks, no pens, no test tube racks, no bubbles, no fizzing, no smoke, no dry ice, no pouring, no splashing, no powder floating in the air, no spilled powder trail, no spoon, no spatula

slots.title: copper-peptide-research — C · tight macro, blue granules and one cylinder, type zone left
slots.prompt:
Tight macro laboratory photograph across a dark bench. In the right half of the frame, at roughly 62 to 80 percent of frame width, one tall plain unmarked clear glass cylinder stands holding a clear vivid blue liquid, colour hex 014EB1, filled about two thirds, perfectly still with a clean meniscus; the key light passes straight through it so the blue glows from within and lays a soft blue caustic across the bench. Behind it and to the right, from 80 to 100 percent of frame width, the objective turret and lower body of one laboratory microscope in matte black and brushed stainless is cropped hard by the right and top edges and thrown out of focus, present but secondary.

In the near foreground at roughly 46 to 64 percent of frame width, a shallow round clear glass laboratory watch dish holds a small conical heap of fine dry crystalline granules in a deep vivid blue, colour hex 014EB1 — coarse, faceted and dense, individual grains resolved and glinting under the raking key light, a few loose grains resting on the glass around the mound. This heap is the closest and sharpest thing in the picture, shot near enough that its texture is fully readable.

Ground and bench are deep graphite, colour hex 1A1A1A, falling to near black, so the blue is the only colour present. One hard key from the upper left, cold and directional, one soft fill. The left 45 percent of the frame, measured from 0 to 45 percent of frame width, is quiet defocused darkness held at even tone and low detail so a headline can sit on it unaided. Shot at f/5.6 on a 100mm macro, clinical and exact.
